# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 2
**Agent:** SOPHIA (Consensus)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 2

---

## Consensus Translation

1. We, the apostles, said to him: "Lord, tell us what is to come — what we will see. How shall we understand the resurrection of the dead? For you speak of great and marvelous things."

2. The Lord showed us a vast garden, full of beautiful trees and blessed fruits, with the fragrance of perfumes upon it. The fragrance was pleasant, and its scent reached us as well.

3. He showed me also an aged man, gleaming in whiteness, and said to me: "This is how it will be at the hour of their need."

4. I, Peter, answered him: "What do you mean? Who is this aged man, and who are the children? And what is this place?"

5. He said to me: "This garden and the trees that you see — these are the righteous dead. The beautiful things you see here represent those who died for the sake of righteousness.

6. The aged man whom you saw is Moses, and the law which God gave him on Mount Sinai.

7. The children are those who died before they had committed sin, who had not yet reached full age. These are in the care of God."

8. He said: "I will show you another mystery. On the day when God judges the world, the righteous will stand before him and the sinners will be on his left.

9. But some of the righteous will shine and some will not — for some have sinned and some have not."

10. I said to him: "I do not understand. Explain it to me."

11. He said: "Those who shine are those who have not sinned and who have done the will of God. Those who do not shine are those who sinned but repented at the end.

12. Among the righteous were those who were poor in this world for God's sake, those who fasted unto God, those who prayed without ceasing, and those who gave freely of their possessions.

13. All of these things will be made known at the resurrection, according to God's will.

14. They will receive the kingdom, the honor, and the glory that God has prepared for those who have feared him."

---

## Textual Notes

- **"Aged man" vs. "ancient man":** SOPHIA prefers "aged" (LOGOS) over EMET's "ancient" — the Greek *presbutēs* connotes age rather than primordial antiquity. The Moses identification is internal to the text.
- **"The care of God" (v.7):** All agents agree; the Ethiopic phrase implies divine guardianship of the unbaptized/sinless young.
- **"Shine" (vv.9–11):** The luminosity motif is important to early Christian eschatology (cf. Dan 12:3, Matt 13:43). All agents preserved it.
- **"For God's sake" (v.12):** The voluntary nature of poverty is stressed — these are ascetic virtues, not involuntary conditions.

---
*SOPHIA synthesis: This chapter introduces the heaven-garden vision that bookends the hell-tour. Consensus renders it with dignity and warmth befitting the paradise imagery.*
